idea.description: Test cross-entropy over one positive and 16 uniformly sampled, distinct negatives per valid causal position in the host-supplied corrected NextItNet. Preserve its backbone, supplied depth-aggregation configuration, scoring head, optimizer and inference architecture. Use matched sampling controls to distinguish objective effects from changes in negative count or exclusion policy. Each configuration independently trains exactly one network per category; deployment loads exactly one selected checkpoint per category without fusion or averaging.
idea.motivation: Explicit competition among multiple alternatives may improve conditional next-item discrimination. The two user-facing targets are broad associations displacing specific matches to current purpose, and older secondary interests outranking recommendations supported by recent interactions. These are hypotheses rather than demonstrated mechanisms: candidate CE can reward predictive conditioning but introduces neither recency weighting nor explicit forgetting, and it can also exploit item-frequency shortcuts. Its user-diagnosis alignment is therefore weaker than the previous rating suggested. The model-facing target is sampled training misranking, reported as 8.22% in Industrial_and_Scientific and 6.67% in Electronics; these position-weighted training observations do not establish held-out error rates. At 20% progress, a controlled loss experiment remains feasible and informative before adding hard mining or architecture changes. Retain causal input suppression as a separate future hypothesis. Historical proposal scores do not establish that CE will outperform the supplied cold start.
idea.implementation_notes:
This is an integration component because the baseline train.py, sample_batch implementation, ModelView and predictor writer are absent from the prompt. Integrate into the supplied corrected baseline rather than inventing its formats, APIs or training harness. The provided loss and sampler helpers are executable components, but their integration placeholders are not a complete runnable train.py. No training, filesystem inspection or new empirical results are claimed here.

Start every configuration from the host-supplied corrected cold start with training seed 42, never another trial's checkpoint. Preserve the supplied architecture, including its actual depth-correction configuration; do not silently import an architecture from the inspiration history. Keep embedding dimensions, convolution blocks, dilation schedule, normalization, masking, final transformation, scorer, optimizer, regularization and gradient processing unchanged for the initial experiment. Baseline training metadata is needed to determine whether the original objective is BCE, BPR or another loss and how its reductions and negative sampler operate. Record those actual settings rather than assuming them.

Use K=16 and temperature=1.0 as the primary proposed configuration. This is uncorrected candidate classification: -log(exp(s_positive)/(exp(s_positive)+sum(exp(s_negative)))). Do not describe it as an unbiased estimator of full-catalog CE or as a calibrated probability over all items. Excluding a user's complete training-item set changes the denominator support to that user's eligible unseen items. For K draws without replacement from M eligible items, each eligible item's inclusion probability is K/M, but adding a correction cannot restore contributions from excluded items. A constant adjustment to every logit cancels; the guaranteed positive and sampled negatives need separate treatment in any future corrected objective. No sampling correction is introduced in this experiment.

Distinguish end-to-end comparison from component attribution. Comparing the native baseline directly with CE16 changes both objective and sampling whenever the native negative count or exclusions differ. It can establish a configuration difference under the pinned metric, but cannot isolate the loss. Before inspecting new scores, record a budget-feasible comparison order: native baseline, native objective with the same K=16 candidate sets and exclusions as CE16, then CE16. If the native objective has no defensible multi-negative extension, specify that explicitly and use a named averaged-BPR16 control rather than calling it the unchanged native objective. For BPR, average softplus(s_negative-s_positive) across valid negatives per position, then across positions. For BCE, separately average the positive term and valid negative terms per position, then sum them; distinguish this class-balanced form from averaging all K+1 labels. Preserve and report the native reduction in the native baseline. Loss scale and regularization balance remain possible explanations when moving between objectives, even with the same optimizer.

If remaining budget permits a prespecified expansion, add CE1 and the corresponding matched one-negative reference, yielding a loss-by-negative-count comparison. Candidate CE1 equals BPR1 at temperature 1, providing an algebraic implementation check rather than a distinct scientific treatment. Generate the K=16 ordered sample first and use its first item for K=1 so samples are nested. Do not simultaneously sweep temperature, architecture, optimizer, exclusions, replacement policy and correction. Replacement, exclusion and correction are separate later questions. If only native baseline and CE16 fit the remaining budget, retain that narrower comparison and explicitly limit attribution. Do not launch a large factorial design simply because related work recommends comprehensive controls.

Sample from mapped, training-observed item IDs only. Exclude padding ID 0, the current target, and every item in the user's complete permitted training history. Never inspect validation or test interactions for exclusions. Including later interactions within the training partition in the exclusion set is an explicit retrospective sampling convention; it is not a causal input feature or a prospective exposure policy. It avoids known-positive collisions but does not eliminate latent false negatives among unseen items. Exclusions also change negative difficulty and may reward frequency shortcuts, so they must match across controlled losses.

Sample uniformly without replacement within each position. Sequential rejection of historical items and already accepted negatives preserves uniform ordered sampling. Do not sort or truncate np.unique results, which can favor smaller IDs. If fewer than K eligible items exist, return all eligible items in random order, pad remaining slots with zero, and mask those slots. If the pool is empty, skip that position and count it. Such shortage rows have fewer competitors and must be reported separately. Do not manufacture negatives, silently switch to replacement, or loop indefinitely. For sparse exclusions, rejection sampling is efficient; after a fixed proposal limit, draw the remainder uniformly from an explicit eligible complement. This preserves uniformity while bounding rejection work. Avoid caching every user's catalog complement or allocating a user-by-catalog dense matrix. Any lazy complement cache must have a documented memory bound. The supplied helper constructs a transient complement only when needed.

Preserve the baseline's sequence/user sampler RNG state and draw order. Use separate randomness for new negative sampling; equal seeds alone do not preserve the original sequence stream. For worker-count-independent negative sampling, derive a NumPy Generator from a SeedSequence containing fixed identifiers: seed 42, declared category index, epoch, batch index and within-batch row occurrence. If training samples individual positions independently, use stable position-occurrence identifiers instead. Repeated occurrences require distinct deterministic identifiers; do not hash Python objects with the process-randomized built-in hash. Match identifiers across loss controls and exclude configuration names from this seed key. Changes in K or rejection cost must not consume sequence-selection randomness.

When the baseline uses a DataLoader, retain its existing sampling behavior and explicitly record its generator and worker initialization. Persistent workers do not rerun worker_init_fn every epoch, so communicate epochs explicitly or use identifier-derived negative generators. import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


CATEGORY_INDEX = {
    'Movies_and_TV': 0,
    'Industrial_and_Scientific': 1,
    'Electronics': 2,
    'CDs_and_Vinyl': 3,
}


def occurrence_rng(category, epoch, batch_index, occurrence_index):
    # Same identifiers across matched loss controls. No Python hash().
    identifiers = [42, CATEGORY_INDEX[category], int(epoch),
                   int(batch_index), int(occurrence_index)]
    if any(x < 0 for x in identifiers):
        raise ValueError('RNG identifiers must be nonnegative')
    return np.random.default_rng(np.random.SeedSequence(identifiers))


def uniform_distinct_negatives(catalog, complete_training_items,
                               target, count, rng):
    """Reference sampler for one valid training position.

    catalog: prevalidated 1-D unique positive training-observed IDs.
    complete_training_items: this user's complete training-item set.
    Returns IDs (count,) and validity mask (count,).
    Production integration should reuse sets and batch worker operations.
    """
    catalog = np.asarray(catalog, dtype=np.int64)
    if catalog.ndim != 1 or count < 1:
        raise ValueError('Expected 1-D catalog and positive count')
    # Validate catalog positivity/uniqueness once at dataset construction.
    forbidden = set(complete_training_items)
    forbidden.add(0)
    forbidden.add(int(target))
    accepted = []
    accepted_set = set()
    proposal_limit = max(64, 8 * count)

    # Preserve acceptance order; never sort np.unique(proposals).
    if len(catalog):
        for _ in range(proposal_limit):
            item = int(catalog[int(rng.integers(len(catalog)))])
            if item in forbidden or item in accepted_set:
                continue
            accepted.append(item)
            accepted_set.add(item)
            if len(accepted) == count:
                break

    if len(accepted) < count:
        # Bounded fallback, transient O(catalog) memory.
        remaining = np.fromiter(
            (int(item) for item in catalog
             if int(item) not in forbidden
             and int(item) not in accepted_set),
            dtype=np.int64,
        )
        take = min(count - len(accepted), len(remaining))
        if take:
            extra = rng.choice(remaining, size=take, replace=False)
            accepted.extend(int(item) for item in extra)

    ids = np.zeros(count, dtype=np.int64)
    valid = np.zeros(count, dtype=np.bool_)
    ids[:len(accepted)] = accepted
    valid[:len(accepted)] = True
    return ids, valid


def matched_candidate_loss(positive_scores, negative_scores,
                           negative_valid, objective='ce',
                           temperature=1.0):
    """Scores come from the unchanged NextItNet predict_score.

    positive_scores: (N,); negative_scores: (N,K).
    Rows represent valid causal training positions.
    Returns mean loss and eligible row count.
    'bce' is explicitly class-balanced, not necessarily native BCE.
    """
    if objective not in ('ce', 'bpr', 'bce'):
        raise ValueError('Unknown objective')
    if temperature <= 0:
        raise ValueError('temperature must be positive')
    if positive_scores.ndim != 1 or negative_scores.ndim != 2:
        raise ValueError('Expected positive (N,) and negative (N,K)')
    if negative_scores.shape[0] != positive_scores.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError('Position counts disagree')
    if negative_valid.shape != negative_scores.shape:
        raise ValueError('Negative mask shape disagrees')
    if negative_valid.dtype != torch.bool:
        raise TypeError('negative_valid must be boolean')

    eligible = negative_valid.any(dim=1)
    count = int(eligible.sum().item())
    if count == 0:
        return positive_scores.sum() * 0.0, 0

    pos = positive_scores[eligible].float() / temperature
    neg = negative_scores[eligible].float() / temperature
    mask = negative_valid[eligible]
    # Remove masked scores before nonlinearities, including possible NaNs.
    neg = neg.masked_fill(~mask, 0.0)
    per_row_count = mask.sum(dim=1).to(pos.dtype)

    if objective == 'ce':
        logits = torch.cat(
            (pos[:, None], neg.masked_fill(~mask, float('-inf'))),
            dim=1,
        )
        labels = torch.zeros(count, dtype=torch.long,
                             device=logits.device)
        return F.cross_entropy(logits, labels), count

    if objective == 'bpr':
        terms = F.softplus(neg - pos[:, None])
        per_row = terms.masked_fill(~mask, 0.0).sum(1)
        per_row = per_row / per_row_count
    else:
        negative_terms = F.softplus(neg).masked_fill(~mask, 0.0)
        per_row = F.softplus(-pos)
        per_row = per_row + negative_terms.sum(1) / per_row_count
    return per_row.mean(), count

originality.positive: The experiment connects matched negative sampling, explicit objective reductions and the required NextItNet diagnostic interfaces in a controlled benchmark adaptation.
originality.negative: Candidate cross-entropy and multi-negative training are established, and NextItNet already discusses sampled softmax. The contribution is experimental evidence rather than a new learning principle.

future_potential.positive: Matched controls can establish whether objective choice or candidate competition deserves further investment before adding retrieval or context-selection mechanisms.
future_potential.negative: Uniform negatives may remain easy, unseen items may be relevant, and sampled validation gains can reflect popularity shortcuts. The method offers no direct solution to stale context, compatibility or purchasing intent.

code_difficulty.positive: The backbone, deployed scorer and checkpoint architecture remain unchanged; the core differentiable loss is small.
code_difficulty.negative: Complete-user exclusions require training-worker provenance, while reproducible RNG separation, matched controls, shortage handling and memory-aware scoring make reliable integration more involved than a loss replacement.

def occurrence_rng(category, epoch, batch_index, occurrence_index):
    # Same identifiers across matched loss controls. No Python hash().
    identifiers = [42, CATEGORY_INDEX[category], int(epoch),
                   int(batch_index), int(occurrence_index)]
    if any(x < 0 for x in identifiers):
        raise ValueError('RNG identifiers must be nonnegative')
    return np.random.default_rng(np.random.SeedSequence(identifiers))


def uniform_distinct_negatives(catalog, complete_training_items,
                               target, count, rng):
    """Reference sampler for one valid training position.

    catalog: prevalidated 1-D unique positive training-observed IDs.
    complete_training_items: this user's complete training-item set.
    Returns IDs (count,) and validity mask (count,).
    Production integration should reuse sets and batch worker operations.
    """
    catalog = np.asarray(catalog, dtype=np.int64)
    if catalog.ndim != 1 or count < 1:
        raise ValueError('Expected 1-D catalog and positive count')
    # Validate catalog positivity/uniqueness once at dataset construction.
    forbidden = set(complete_training_items)
    forbidden.add(0)
    forbidden.add(int(target))
    accepted = []
    accepted_set = set()
    proposal_limit = max(64, 8 * count)

    # Preserve acceptance order; never sort np.unique(proposals).
    if len(catalog):
        for _ in range(proposal_limit):
            item = int(catalog[int(rng.integers(len(catalog)))])
            if item in forbidden or item in accepted_set:
                continue
            accepted.append(item)
            accepted_set.add(item)
            if len(accepted) == count:
                break

    if len(accepted) < count:
        # Bounded fallback, transient O(catalog) memory.
        remaining = np.fromiter(
            (int(item) for item in catalog
             if int(item) not in forbidden
             and int(item) not in accepted_set),
            dtype=np.int64,
        )
        take = min(count - len(accepted), len(remaining))
        if take:
            extra = rng.choice(remaining, size=take, replace=False)
            accepted.extend(int(item) for item in extra)

    ids = np.zeros(count, dtype=np.int64)
    valid = np.zeros(count, dtype=np.bool_)
    ids[:len(accepted)] = accepted
    valid[:len(accepted)] = True
    return ids, valid


def matched_candidate_loss(positive_scores, negative_scores,
                           negative_valid, objective='ce',
                           temperature=1.0):
    """Scores come from the unchanged NextItNet predict_score.

    positive_scores: (N,); negative_scores: (N,K).
    Rows represent valid causal training positions.
    Returns mean loss and eligible row count.
    'bce' is explicitly class-balanced, not necessarily native BCE.
    """
    if objective not in ('ce', 'bpr', 'bce'):
        raise ValueError('Unknown objective')
    if temperature <= 0:
        raise ValueError('temperature must be positive')
    if positive_scores.ndim != 1 or negative_scores.ndim != 2:
        raise ValueError('Expected positive (N,) and negative (N,K)')
    if negative_scores.shape[0] != positive_scores.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError('Position counts disagree')
    if negative_valid.shape != negative_scores.shape:
        raise ValueError('Negative mask shape disagrees')
    if negative_valid.dtype != torch.bool:
        raise TypeError('negative_valid must be boolean')

    eligible = negative_valid.any(dim=1)
    count = int(eligible.sum().item())
    if count == 0:
        return positive_scores.sum() * 0.0, 0

    pos = positive_scores[eligible].float() / temperature
    neg = negative_scores[eligible].float() / temperature
    mask = negative_valid[eligible]
    # Remove masked scores before nonlinearities, including possible NaNs.
    neg = neg.masked_fill(~mask, 0.0)
    per_row_count = mask.sum(dim=1).to(pos.dtype)

    if objective == 'ce':
        logits = torch.cat(
            (pos[:, None], neg.masked_fill(~mask, float('-inf'))),
            dim=1,
        )
        labels = torch.zeros(count, dtype=torch.long,
                             device=logits.device)
        return F.cross_entropy(logits, labels), count

    if objective == 'bpr':
        terms = F.softplus(neg - pos[:, None])
        per_row = terms.masked_fill(~mask, 0.0).sum(1)
        per_row = per_row / per_row_count
    else:
        negative_terms = F.softplus(neg).masked_fill(~mask, 0.0)
        per_row = F.softplus(-pos)
        per_row = per_row + negative_terms.sum(1) / per_row_count
    return per_row.mean(), count

Establish which faults the probes detect, with explicit activation and detection denominators, before using diagnostic health to motivate costly training interventions. Do not assume dot-product scoring when the implementation differs. Exercise all four category routes, unequal batch/candidate dimensions, singleton dimensions and boundary valid item IDs. Predeclare a small operator registry with exact mutation locations and behavior: substitute count_nonzero-1 for endpoint selection; introduce a future-token dependency at an intermediate valid position; shift or swap valid item indices in exactly one pipeline component; and alter one supported scorer/export operation. Include transpose and omitted-bias variants only when tensor shapes and an actual nonzero bias make them valid. Do not invent a bias absent from the model. Future-access mutation is assessed at intermediate positions, since the final endpoint has no future history token. Record changed source/configuration, applicable graph requirements and expected invariant for every operator.

Separate development operators from held-out evaluation implementations before observing results. For example, develop a mapping-offset check and reserve an in-range row swap; development and evaluation operators must remain valid under the actual vocabulary. If the available implementation supports only one mutation per class, report that limitation and make no claim of generalization across fault implementations. Do not tune probes against held-out operators after evaluation. Add independently confirmed implementation faults only when already available within the authorized supplied baseline context; do not inspect other trials, fabricate bugs, or deliberately retain faults in production. Otherwise real-fault detection, localization/repair success and incremental real-bug utility remain unavailable future outcomes.

Audit one component mutation at a time on disposable copies. For each user/operator case, record attempted, valid, reached, infected, output-changing and detected indicators separately. Valid means executable and consistent with the operator specification; reached means the changed computation executed; infected means the intended intermediate state or index differs; output-changing means raw scores differ beyond the frozen tolerance, with rank/top-ten changes separately recorded under a declared ascending-item-ID tie order. Detected means a predefined diagnostic alarm fired. Verify activation with structural instrumentation or independent expected values, rather than using the evaluation alarm as its sole witness. Witness-user activation does not establish infection for every evaluation user: measure these indicators per evaluation case. Unreached, untriggered or behaviorally unchanged sampled cases are not proven semantically equivalent mutants.

Run identical declared checks on clean and mutated cases. Clean controls include batch permutation, candidate permutation with corresponding inverse score reordering, identical-input repeatability, supported checkpoint reload equivalence, independently specified endpoint fixtures, causal-prefix invariance and supported independent scoring/mapping checks. Batch and candidate permutations test consistency, not semantic correctness. Arbitrary history permutation, deletion and extra padding are not assumed invariant. Preserve the original training negative distribution and objective; this audit changes neither.

For each category/fault class, report attempted, valid, reached, infected, output-changing and detected case counts, along with missingness. Define activation coverage as infected/valid; primary conditional score-fault sensitivity as detected-and-output-changing/output-changing; state-infection sensitivity as detected-and-infected/infected; and end-to-end yield as detected/valid. State the target of each detector and never interchange these estimands. Separately report alarms on valid mutants without output changes and clean-control alarms/eligible clean cases. Specificity equals one minus the corresponding clean false-alarm rate. Zero denominators yield null with reasons. Do not label user-case detection a traditional mutation score. If reporting distinct killed-mutant counts, define killing and the mutant universe explicitly; do not claim a denominator of nonequivalent mutants without defensible equivalence adjudication.

Show category/class counts and paired differences in detection relative to the existing adapter on identical cases. Separate additional detections from additional false alarms. With fixed mutant implementations, optional 2,000-draw seed-42 bootstrap intervals resample users within category and retain every user's controls, operators and outputs together. These intervals describe user variability conditional on fixed models/operators and can degenerate when events are absent. For an explicitly defined single independent Bernoulli outcome per user, report Wilson or exact Clopper-Pearson intervals instead. For zero events among n independent eligible users, the one-sided 95% upper bound is 1-0.05^(1/n), approximately 8.94% at n=32; zero misses correspond to sensitivity at least 91.06%. Do not apply these bounds to pooled dependent cases or to a 16-user evaluation subset using n=32. Repeated users do not supply mutant replication, and one operator per class cannot estimate operator variability.

Retain existing bounded diagnostic metrics and definitions, including their training-only limitations. Calibration may be capped independently of the existing 200-user behavioral panels. Do not pool heterogeneous fault classes into a universal reliability probability. Model-selection shortcuts include adapting tolerances to mutants, selecting only easily activated cases, reusing development operators as independent evaluation and using the same helper in both oracle and implementation. Record these dependencies and avoid post-hoc claims. The twenty-user qualitative panel remains descriptive, and compatibility, ownership, intent and simulator traits remain unobserved unless explicit supplied evidence supports a particular statement.

Preserve every module's original mode and global Python, NumPy, Torch CPU and relevant CUDA RNG states in finally; use local generators, evaluation mode and no_grad. Restore hooks and wrappers even on failure and release each disposable copy before creating another. Never accumulate parameter gradients or modify the optimizer. Bound work to the declared user/operator registry, one mutation copy at a time, and no additional fitting. Record synchronized GPU elapsed time, forward/scoring counts, peak memory with measurement scope, and artifact-writing time. If budget is insufficient, mark unfinished operators unavailable rather than silently selecting favorable ones. Report incremental diagnostic GPU overhead; no additional retraining is required by this proposal. Any later repair/retraining and failed trials must also count against the shared budget.

Keep all artifacts beneath the trial directory and retain DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution, supplied splits and pinned evaluator. Train one independent corrected NextItNet model per category and retain exactly one production checkpoint per category. No independently fitted auxiliary scorer, fusion, averaging or mutated copy enters inference. The diagnostic-only change leaves the production architecture and predictor writer unchanged, while testing their actual outputs where available. Future architecture changes must update both consistently. Use no hidden tests, other-trial checkpoints, external datasets or pretrained weights. class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        state = save_all_module_modes_and_global_rng_states(self.view.model)
        metrics, definitions = existing_diagnostic_schema()
        resources = begin_synchronized_resource_accounting()
        try:
            self.view.model.eval()
            provenance = record_explicit_category_checkpoint_and_interfaces()
            users = select_sorted_identified_training_users(seed=42, cap=32)
            witness_users, evaluation_users = split_at_floor_half(users)
            fixtures = independently_specified_endpoint_mapping_and_causal_fixtures()
            rules = freeze_rules_on_correct_fixtures_before_mutant_evaluation(fixtures)
            operators = freeze_valid_development_and_held_out_operator_registry()
            with torch.no_grad():
                run_existing_bounded_diagnostics(train_loader)
                record_unsupported_references_as_null_with_reasons()
                clean_records = run_existing_and_augmented_checks(
                    production_view=self.view,
                    actual_exported_predictor=available_predictor_or_none(),
                    independent_references=fixtures,
                    users=evaluation_users,
                    rules=rules
                )
                for operator in operators:
                    disposable_view = None
                    try:
                        disposable_view = isolate_one_unfitted_copy(self.view)
                        validity = apply_exactly_one_supported_mutation(disposable_view, operator)
                        if not validity.supported:
                            record_unsupported_operator(operator, validity.reason)
                            continue
                        record_separate_witness_checks(
                            disposable_view, self.view, witness_users, operator
                        )
                        for user in evaluation_users:
                            case = construct_fixed_training_prefix_and_candidates(user)
                            trace = instrument_reach_and_state_infection(
                                disposable_view, self.view, operator, case
                            )
                            output_change = compare_raw_scores_ranks_and_top10(
                                disposable_view, self.view, case, rules
                            )
                            alarms = run_existing_and_augmented_checks_on_same_case(
                                disposable_view, fixtures, case, rules
                            )
                            record_case_indicators(
                                attempted=True, valid=validity,
                                reached=trace.reached, infected=trace.infected,
                                output_changing=output_change, detected=alarms
                            )
                    finally:
                        remove_mutation_hooks_and_release_copy(disposable_view)
                summarize_by_category_operator_and_detector_with_exact_denominators()
                compare_additional_detections_and_false_alarms_against_existing_checks()
                bootstrap_complete_user_clusters_if_informative(draws=2000, seed=42)
                add_binomial_intervals_only_for_declared_independent_user_outcomes()
                record_unavailable_real_fault_and_operator_generalization_evidence()
        finally:
            restore_all_module_modes_hooks_and_global_rng_states(state)
            record_synchronized_runtime_memory_and_forward_counts(resources)
        return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}

report:
Test **16-negative candidate cross-entropy with the corrected NextItNet architecture fixed**, while strengthening controls before attributing gains to the objective. At 20% progress, this remains more practical than hard-negative retrieval or additional context gates.

Three starting-point insights guide the experiment. First, zero-initialized residual-depth correction preserves the final-state path initially, supporting controlled architecture comparisons. Second, reported scores of 0.5325 and 0.5175 motivate retaining existing features, but lack paired uncertainty. Third, Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics show 8.22% and 6.67% sampled training misranking. These descriptive observations motivate discrimination experiments without establishing held-out weakness or temporal causes.

Three literature insights refine the methodology. NextItNet and Scalable Cross-Entropy motivate studying candidate competition, but establish no winner here. Di Teodoro et al. show that one-negative candidate CE equals BPR; Wu et al. motivate separating objective, negative count and sampling. PSL and R2NS caution against false negatives and unrestrained hardness, supporting uniform sampling first. MSDCCL motivates later suppression experiments, because changing discrimination does not directly remove stale context.

| Direction | Intervention | Unresolved question |
|---|---|---|
| Representation | Residual-depth correction | Are intermediate depths useful? |
| Discrimination | Multi-negative cross-entropy | Does competition improve specific matches? |
| Context | Causal input suppression | Can stale context be reduced safely? |

Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Every dimension includes a favorable and unfavorable assessment.

|---|---|---|
| **Uniform 16-negative CE** [NextItNet, SCE, Di Teodoro] | 2/6/4/7/4 | Originality: controlled adaptation, established objective. Potential: reusable evidence, uncertain transfer.                         view.predict_score(intact_features, cand_t)
                        .detach()
                        .float()
                        .cpu()
                        .numpy()
                    )
                    if baseline.shape != (99,) or not np.isfinite(baseline).all():
                        raise RuntimeError(
                            "Diagnostic scorer must return 99 finite candidate scores"
                        )
                    variants, labels, geometry = (
                        [intact.copy()],
                        ["identity"],
                        [{"changed": 0}],
                    )
                    unavailable = Counter()

                    def add(label, history, metadata):
                        array = padded(history)
                        if np.array_equal(array, intact):
                            unavailable[label + ":unchanged"] += 1
                            return
                        variants.append(array)
                        labels.append(label)
                        geometry.append(metadata)

                    for fraction in (0.25, 0.5):
                        n = len(h)
                        k = max(1, int(fraction * len(original)))
                        prefix = str(fraction) + ":"
                        if n <= k:
                            unavailable[prefix + "insufficient_remaining_history"] += 1
                            continue
                        regions = {"recent": np.arange(n - k, n)}
                        if n - k >= k:
                            regions["old"] = np.arange(k)
                        else:
                            unavailable[prefix + "old:cannot_preserve_newest_k"] += 1
                        if n - k >= k:
                            regions["random"] = np.sort(
                                rng.choice(n - k, k, replace=False)
                            )
                        else:
                            unavailable[prefix + "random:cannot_preserve_newest_k"] += 1
                        if n - k - 1 >= k:
                            regions["interior"] = np.sort(
                                rng.choice(np.arange(1, n - k), k, replace=False)
                            )
                        else:
                            unavailable[
                                prefix + "interior:cannot_preserve_newest_k"
                            ] += 1
                        for name, positions in regions.items():
                            metadata = {
                                "k": k,
                                "original_length": len(original),
                                "retained_length": n,
                                "input_width": maxlen,
                                "lags": (n - 1 - positions).tolist(),
                                "newest_k_preserved": bool(np.all(positions < n - k)),
                            }
                            add(
                                prefix + name + "_delete",
                                np.delete(h, positions),
                                metadata,
                            )
                            zeros = h.copy()
                            zeros[positions] = 0
                            add(prefix + name + "_zero", zeros, metadata)
                            replacements = h.copy()
                            unmatched = 0
                            for p in positions:
                                forbidden = np.concatenate((h, candidates))
                                options = pools[decile[int(h[p])]]
                                options = options[~np.isin(options, forbidden)]
                                if not len(options):
                                    unmatched += 1
                                    options = observed[~np.isin(observed, forbidden)]
                                if not len(options):
                                    break
                                replacements[p] = rng.choice(options)
                            else:
                                add(
                                    prefix + name + "_replace",
                                    replacements,
                                    dict(
                                        metadata, unmatched_frequency_decile=unmatched
                                    ),
                                )
                                continue
                            unavailable[prefix + name + "_replace:no_alternative"] += 1
                        for name, positions in (
                            ("recent", np.arange(n - k, n)),
                            ("old", np.arange(n - k)),
                        ):
                            if len(positions) < 2 or len(np.unique(h[positions])) < 2:
                                unavailable[
                                    prefix
                                    + name
                                    + "_shuffle:insufficient_distinct_items"
                                ] += 1
                                continue
                            for draw in range(20):
                                altered = h.copy()
                                altered[positions] = rng.permutation(h[positions])
                                add(
                                    prefix + name + "_shuffle",
                                    altered,
                                    {
                                        "k": k,
                                        "region_size": len(positions),
                                        "draw": draw,
                                        "lags": (n - 1 - positions).tolist(),
                                        "retained_length": n,
                                        "input_width": maxlen,
                                    },
                                )
                    scores = score_vectors(variants, cand_t)
                    if (
                        scores.shape != (len(variants), 99)
                        or not np.isfinite(scores).all()
                    ):
                        raise RuntimeError(
                            "Diagnostic intervention scores have invalid shape or nonfinite values"
                        )
                    effects = {}
                    for label in dict.fromkeys(labels):
                        indices = [
                            i for i, label_i in enumerate(labels) if label_i == label
                        ]
                        delta = scores[indices] - baseline
                        effects[label] = {
                            "mean_absolute_score_change": float(np.abs(delta).mean()),
                            "signed_mean_score_change": float(delta.mean()),
                            "changed_draws": len(indices),
                            "geometry": [geometry[i] for i in indices],
                        }
                    user_rows.append(
                        {
                            "user_id": str(uid),
                            "original_length": len(original),
                            "retained_length": len(h),
                            "effects": effects,
                            "ineligible": dict(unavailable),
                        }
                    )

                metrics["intact_user_endpoint_representations"] = (
                    representation(torch.stack(intact_user_states))
                    if intact_user_states
                    else {
                        "count": 0,
                        "value": None,
                        "reason": "No eligible identified training users",
                    }
                )
                definitions["intact_user_endpoint_representations"] = (
                    "Raw and unit-normalized covariance statistics and norm quantiles for "
                    "one intact final-nonpadding feature per identified training user "
                    "eligible for the fixed-candidate sensitivity probe. Loader endpoint "
                    "statistics remain separate and may contain repeated users."
                )
                definitions["paired_contrasts"] = (
                    "Within-user difference between each named method and the first method "
                    "in its declared comparison family, computed on common eligible users. "
                    "Bootstrap intervals resample each complete paired vector together. "
                    "These are score-sensitivity contrasts, not ranking improvements."
                )

                sensitivity_bootstrap_weights = {}

                def aggregate(rows, names):
                    if not rows:
                        return {
                            "eligible_users": 0,
                            "estimates": None,
                            "reason": "No common eligible users",
                        }
                    columns = [
                        (name, field)
                        for name in names
                        for field in (
                            "mean_absolute_score_change",
                            "signed_mean_score_change",
                        )
                    ]
                    values = np.asarray(
                        [
                            [r["effects"][name][field] for name, field in columns]
                            for r in rows
                        ]
                    )
                    # Reuse deterministic user multiplicities by cohort size.
                    # Every column still shares the same paired resample.
                    n = len(rows)
                    if n not in sensitivity_bootstrap_weights:
                        draws = np.random.default_rng(42).integers(n, size=(2000, n))
                        counts = np.zeros((2000, n), dtype=np.float64)
                        np.add.at(counts, (np.arange(2000)[:, None], draws), 1.0)
                        sensitivity_bootstrap_weights[n] = counts / n
                    means = sensitivity_bootstrap_weights[n] @ values
                    bounds = np.quantile(means, [0.025, 0.975], axis=0)
                    contrasts = {}
                    for j, (name, field) in enumerate(columns):
                        if name == names[0]:
                            continue
                        reference = columns.index((names[0], field))
                        paired_difference = values[:, j] - values[:, reference]
                        bootstrap_difference = means[:, j] - means[:, reference]
                        contrasts[name + "_minus_" + names[0] + ":" + field] = {
                            "mean": float(paired_difference.mean()),
                            "ci95": np.quantile(
                                bootstrap_difference, [0.025, 0.975]
                            ).tolist(),
                        }
                    return {
                        "eligible_users": len(rows),
                        "paired_contrasts": contrasts,
                        "estimates": {
                            name
                            + ":"
                            + field: {
                                "mean": float(values[:, j].mean()),
                                "ci95": bounds[:, j].tolist(),
                            }
                            for j, (name, field) in enumerate(columns)
                        },
                    }

                groups = {
                    "all": lambda r: True,
                    "1-10": lambda r: r["original_length"] <= 10,
                    "11-25": lambda r: 11 <= r["original_length"] <= 25,
                    "26+": lambda r: r["original_length"] >= 26,
                }
                methods = ["identity"] + [
                    str(fraction) + ":" + suffix
                    for fraction in (0.25, 0.5)
                    for suffix in (
                        "old_delete",
                        "recent_delete",
                        "random_delete",
                        "interior_delete",
                        "old_zero",
                        "recent_zero",
                        "random_zero",
                        "interior_zero",
                        "old_replace",
                        "recent_replace",
                        "random_replace",
                        "interior_replace",
                        "old_shuffle",
                        "recent_shuffle",
                    )
                ]
                aggregates, common = {}, {}
                for group, predicate in groups.items():
                    rows = [r for r in user_rows if predicate(r)]
                    aggregates[group] = {
                        name: aggregate(
                            [r for r in rows if name in r["effects"]], [name]
                        )
                        for name in methods
                    }
                    common[group] = {}
                    for fraction in (0.25, 0.5):
                        prefix = str(fraction) + ":"
                        families = {
                            "deletions": [
                                "old_delete",
                                "recent_delete",
                                "random_delete",
                                "interior_delete",
                            ],
                            "old_geometry_controls": [
                                "old_delete",
                                "old_zero",
                                "old_replace",
                            ],
                            "recent_geometry_controls": [
                                "recent_delete",
                                "recent_zero",
                                "recent_replace",
                            ],
                            "random_geometry_controls": [
                                "random_delete",
                                "random_zero",
                                "random_replace",
                            ],
                            "interior_geometry_controls": [
                                "interior_delete",
                                "interior_zero",
                                "interior_replace",
                            ],
                            "shuffles": ["old_shuffle", "recent_shuffle"],
                        }
                        for family, suffixes in families.items():
                            names = [prefix + suffix for suffix in suffixes]
                            paired = [
                                r
                                for r in rows
                                if all(name in r["effects"] for name in names)
                            ]
                            common[group][prefix + family] = aggregate(paired, names)
                metrics["user_score_sensitivity"] = {
                    "category": str(
                        getattr(
                            view,
                            "dataset_name",
                            getattr(network, "dataset_name", "current_category"),
                        )
                    ),
                    "selected_users": len(chosen),
                    "eligible_users": len(user_rows),
                    "skipped_users": dict(skips),
                    "maxlen": maxlen,
                    "candidate_source": "99 fixed training-observed unseen IDs per identified user",
                    "by_original_length": aggregates,
                    "common_eligible_comparisons": common,
                    "paired_user_records": user_rows,
                }
                calibration = calibrate_adapter(view, self.device)
                metrics["adapter_calibration"] = calibration
                definitions["adapter_calibration"] = (
                    "Diagnostic-only synthetic fault calibration on at most 32 identified "
                    "training users, with lexicographically sorted canonical IDs and local "
                    "seed-42 selection. The first floor(n/2) selected users are witnesses; "
                    "the remainder are evaluation users. Tolerances are fixed before "
                    "execution. Valid, reached, infected, output-changing and detected "
                    "are separate case indicators. Old checks are repeatability, batch "
                    "reordering and intermediate causal-prefix invariance; augmented "
                    "checks additionally compare independently selected endpoint features "
                    "and explicit tied-dot-product scores. Conditional sensitivity uses "
                    "output-changing cases, infection sensitivity uses infected cases, "
                    "and yield uses valid cases. Zero denominators are unavailable. "
                    "Clean alarms and additional detections are reported separately. "
                    "Mapping mutations affect input lookup only. Copies are unfitted, "
                    "never saved and never used for production. These are training-prefix "
                    "cases, not validation observations. Fixed synthetic operators do not "
                    "establish real-fault utility or operator generalization. Reference "
                    "and export limitations are recorded explicitly."
                )
                metrics["candidate_depth_audit"] = self._candidate_depth_audit()
                definitions["candidate_depth_audit"] = (
                    "In-sample exploratory training-prefix audit; no validation labels. "
                    "Up to 200 uniformly sampled eligible users without replacement, sorted "
                    "before selection; seed 42 plus declared category index and stable hashed "
                    "user ID for ten independent candidate repetitions. Unknown category uses "
                    "index 4 and must not be treated as a named category macro report. Each "
                    "target is the final permitted training interaction; its cutoff is a zero-based "
                    "training index, and it may have been optimized during fitting. Prefixes are "
                    "left-padded/truncated to model.maxlen and read at the largest nonzero index. "
                    "The catalog contains only mapped training-observed items. Negative pools "
                    "exclude every full training-history item, including target; this is retrospective "
                    "hindsight rather than a prospective exclusion policy. Repeated targets are "
                    "recorded before exclusion. Ten uniform ordered samples without replacement "
                    "share nested prefixes of 99/499/999 negatives. Missing depths are unavailable, "
                    "with counts in user-repetition-depth units. Ties favor ascending item ID. "
                    "Rank includes the positive; hit means rank<=10. Margin subtracts the tenth "
                    "largest negative score and is scale dependent. Nested ranks cannot improve "
                    "with depth; declining hit rates alone imply nothing about generalization. "
                    "Users receive equal weight; depth-specific populations may differ. Paired "
                    "comparisons use common eligible users and 2000 seed-42 user-cluster bootstrap "
                    "resamples conditional on candidate repetition zero. Intervals exclude training "
                    "seed, adaptive search and candidate-resampling uncertainty. Repetition SD is "
                    "computed across ten category-level summaries; SD/sqrt(10) is solely Monte "
                    "Carlo error of their average, with model and users fixed. Repetitions are never "
                    "independent users. Frequency bands use all valid permitted training interactions, "
                    "descending frequency then ascending item ID: first ceil(20%) head, next through "
                    "ceil(50%) middle, remainder tail. Length bins use prefixes before truncation. "
                    "At most 50 randomly selected audit users have exact full-eligible-pool ranks; "
                    "scores stream in chunks<=4096 and retain only the top ten negative items. "
                    "N is eligible negative count and M counts negatives preceding the target. "
                    "Conditional expected hit is hypergeom.cdf(9,N,M,m); expected rank is "
                    "1+m*M/N, applicable only to declared uniform sampling and tie order. "
                    "Expected/observed residuals measure sampling variability, not generalization. "
                    "Recommendation popularity and catalog coverage describe top-ten scores on "
                    "these same restricted negative pools, excluding known training items and the "
                    "target; they are not unrestricted-catalog recommendation quality. Existing "
                    "controlled shuffle/truncation probes remain descriptive controls. Only one "
                    "category is measured here; four-category macro summaries require all four "
                    "reports and equal category weights. No auxiliary scorer or model is fitted."
                )
                metrics["four_category_macro"] = {
                    "value": None,
                    "reason": "This ModelView contains one category; aggregate four category reports externally only when all four have eligible observations",
                }
                metrics["validation_interventions"] = {
                    "value": None,
                    "reason": "No authorized pinned validation user/target/candidate interface supplied",
                }
                metrics["pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown"] = {
                    "value": None,
                    "reason": "Item categories are unavailable in this benchmark",
                }
                metrics["unobserved_traits"] = [
                    "ratings",
                    "review text",
                    "prices",
                    "stores",
                    "item categories",
                    "simulator diversity",
                    "simulator conformity",
                ]
                metrics["diagnostic_scope"] = (
                    "Exploratory diagnostics only; no model, checkpoint, sampling, training, predictor or evaluator changes"
                )
        finally:
            for module, mode in previous_modes:
                module.training = mode
            random.setstate(python_state)
            np.random.set_state(numpy_state)
            torch.random.set_rng_state(torch_state)
            if cuda_state is not None:
                torch.cuda.set_rng_state_all(cuda_state)
        if self.device.type == "cuda":
            torch.cuda.synchronize(self.device)
        metrics["diagnostic_elapsed_seconds"] = time.perf_counter() - diagnostic_started
        definitions["diagnostic_elapsed_seconds"] = (
            "Wall-clock seconds for all probes, including exact eligible-pool scoring "
            "and final CUDA synchronization; prior queued CUDA work is excluded by "
            "synchronizing before timing. Diagnostic execution consumes the shared "
            "experiment budget."
        )
        return {"metrics": metrics, "metric_definitions": definitions}
